facts.text: The simulation node sets xml_path to resources/go2/scene_terrain.xml under the project root and loads it with mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path.
scene_terrain.xml includes go2.xml.

The simulator declares a LowState publisher on /mujoco/lowstate, a Float32MultiArray publisher on /mujoco/pos, a Float32MultiArray publisher on /mujoco/torque and a LowCmd subscription on /mujoco/lowcmd.
The simulation node imports LowState and LowCmd from unitree_go.msg.
The simulation node imports Float32MultiArray from std_msgs.msg.
target_torque_callback sets recieve_data true on every LowCmd, then copies motor_cmd[i].q, .kp and .kd for i in 0..11 into target_dof_pos, kps and kds; no other MotorCmd field is read.
update_tau returns until recieve_data is true and then computes tau[i] with pd_control from target_dof_pos[i], qpos[7+i], kps[i], qvel[6+i] and kds[i] for each of the twelve motors.
pd_control returns (target_q - q) * kp - dq * kd.
The node creates a 2 ms timer for publish_sensor_data and a 1 ms timer for update_tau, and starts step_simulation in its own thread.

step_simulation loops while the viewer runs and running is true; until recieve_data is true it continues without sleeping, and afterwards it copies tau into d.ctrl, publishes it on /mujoco/torque, calls mujoco.mj_step and sleeps for the rest of the model timestep, with no check for a fresh LowCmd.
publish_sensor_data copies motor_state[i].q and .dq for i in 0..11 from qpos[7+i] and qvel[6+i], copies qpos[3:7] into imu_state.quaternion and sensordata[40:43] into imu_state.gyroscope.
publish_sensor_data publishes d.qpos[:19] as the Float32MultiArray data on /mujoco/pos.
The node sets the MuJoCo timestep to 0.005 s.
stop_simulation sets running false and joins the simulation thread.
main() calls stop_simulation and viewer.close() only in its finally block after rclpy.spin.
The MuJoCo model declares per-class joint ranges: abduction -1.0472 to 1.0472 rad, front hip -1.5708 to 3.4907 rad, back hip -0.5236 to 4.5379 rad and knee -2.7227 to -0.83776 rad.
The model's actuator block lists the twelve motors in FR, FL, RR, RL leg order, three joints per leg.
The go2 default class sets the motor ctrlrange to -23.7 to 23.7, and the knee class overrides it to -45.43 to 45.43.

low_level_ctrl declares is_simulation with default true; in simulation mode it publishes LowCmd on /mujoco/lowcmd and subscribes to LowState on /mujoco/lowstate, and otherwise it uses /lowcmd and /lowstate.
low_level_ctrl creates a 5 ms wall timer that runs state_machine.
state_machine's hold branch sets mode 0x01 and the standing or lay-down target angles with kp and kd for the twelve motors, computes the CRC and publishes the LowCmd.
low_level_ctrl's run_policy writes the target positions with kp 30 and kd 0.75 for all twelve motors.
target_pos_callback calls run_policy only while is_standing_ and should_run_policy_ are both true; otherwise it only stores the received target vector.
joy_callback calls rclcpp::shutdown() when joystick axes 2 and 5 are both -1.
rl_policy.py subscribes to /mujoco/lowstate when args.simulation is set and to /lowstate otherwise.
rl_policy.py publishes its target joint positions as a Float32MultiArray on /rl/target_pos.
rl_policy.py reorders the measured joint vectors with sequence [3, 4, 5, 0, 1, 2, 9, 10, 11, 6, 7, 8]; the comment above the two reorder lines says to comment them out for simulation.
The shipped policy configuration sets num_actions 12 and action_scale 0.25.
The README runs the MuJoCo simulator with ros2 run deploy_rl_policy mujoco_simulator.py.
The README describes low_level_control as the 3-state machine that sends lowcmd to the simulator or the real robot.
The README maps joystick B, A and LB+RB to stand up, lay down and execute the RL policy.
The README instructs the operator to turn down the robot's sport mode service before deploying a policy on the real robot; that service is not implemented in this clone.

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned replies with no physics step, no PD integration and no wall-clock pacing; placeholder samples do not establish trajectory or state-hash replay

fidelity.engine: analytic:ROS contract fake (canned replies; no MuJoCo physics)
gaps: the fake is a ROS-free RecordingRosTransport: it answers the declared endpoints with placeholder messages and runs no MuJoCo model, no PD law, no contacts, no ROS node and no wall-clock loop
the LowCmd publication is recorded only; the fake does not compute torque, integrate the model or prove that a command was received, executed or stopped
the published /mujoco/lowstate and /mujoco/pos samples are placeholders; a live run must receive the simulator's actual 500 Hz LowState and 2 ms qpos publications
the fake returns the full 20-slot motor_state arrays and the 4-value quaternion that the ROS message declares; only the first twelve motor slots are filled by the simulator
the upstream model timestep is 0.005 s and the node timers are 2 ms and 1 ms; these are source facts, not fake timing
the node declares /mujoco/force but never publishes it (the publish call is commented out); that topic is not bound

the e-stop is a sensed-confirmation stop (SAFE-049, simulated only): one passive LowCmd on /mujoco/lowcmd, confirmed only by twelve /mujoco/lowstate joint velocities and the span of /mujoco/pos data[0..2], both arrival freshness with min_interval_ms 1 (publishers at mujoco_simulator.py:20-21). Both topics are on the 2 ms timer at :33, so three samples span 4 ms (min_span_ms 4). The 1 ms timer at :34 does not publish them. A slower timer still meets the arrival window while the gap stays under max_gap_ms 500; a stream closer than 1 ms restarts the count

low_level_ctrl's 5 ms state machine overwrites /mujoco/lowcmd (low_level_ctrl.cpp:63, 148-167). Silence, a subscription error, nonzero holding gains, and a sample the exclusion ring drops each refuse the confirmation. The keep branch publishes nothing when that controller is absent, so this stop has no source-backed controller stop. With is_simulation false the same node publishes /lowcmd, which this package does not bind
the first /mujoco/pos sample sets data[2] from the publication count so a LowCmd has an observable effect; counted confirmation samples use a fixed rest pose, not that echo
the /rl/target_pos policy path, the joystick /joy input and the C++ low_level_ctrl state machine are not bound; they are cited as source facts only

low_level_ctrl, which the README runs next to the simulator, publishes LowCmd on /mujoco/lowcmd every 5 ms from its state machine, so while it runs any LowCmd from this package is overwritten within 5 ms; with is_simulation false the same node commands /lowcmd, the README's real-robot path, which this package never binds
